title: Open WebUI automation recurrence -- T1499 fixed-epoch minutely rule walks ~25 years synchronously
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70489 (GHSA-73cq-mcgh-379c,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI from 0.9.0 until 0.11.0.

Automation recurrence parsing (`backend/open_webui/utils/automations.py`)
anchored MINUTELY and HOURLY rules at a fixed epoch date of
`2000-01-01` and walked forward one interval at a time to find the next
run relative to now. A single user-submitted `FREQ=MINUTELY` automation
rule therefore enumerates roughly a QUARTER-CENTURY of occurrences,
one minute at a time, SYNCHRONOUSLY on the same event loop that also
serves scheduler, HTTP, and WebSocket traffic for every other user of
the instance. Worse, the scheduler recomputes this same walk for every
claimed row on each poll cycle -- a single malicious automation rule
degrades or blocks the entire instance's responsiveness for all users,
not just its own creator.

Detection logic flags the creation of an automation with a
`FREQ=MINUTELY` or `FREQ=HOURLY` recurrence rule -- the specific rule
granularity the fixed-epoch walk makes catastrophically expensive; a
`FREQ=DAILY` or coarser rule does not trigger the same magnitude of
enumeration.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact source file), fixed in 0.11.0.
